mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 2.5% year-over-year signals inflationary pressures that may lead to tighter monetary policy, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If CPIAUCSL YoY > 2.5% and S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% in one month signals economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If UNRATE rises > 0.5% in 1 month and S&P 500 forward 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) over three months signals strengthening consumer demand, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If HOUST increases > 5% over 3 months and S&P 500 forward 60-day returns are negative in more than 40% of instances, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% month-over-month signals supply-side weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If INDPRO decreases > 2% MoM and S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is below 1% and CPIAUCSL YoY is above 3%, the combination signals a potential overheating economy with loose monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS < 1% and CPIAUCSL YoY > 3% and S&P 500 forward 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 300,000 in a month signals strong labor market conditions, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If PAYEMS increases > 300,000 in a month and S&P 500 forward 5-day returns are negative in more than 40% of instances, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: When real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) grow faster than GDP (GDPC1) over a quarter, it signals robust consumer demand, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS growth > GDPC1 growth over 1 quarter
failure_condition: If RSAFS growth > GDPC1 growth over 1 quarter and S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are negative in more than 40% of instances, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) signals an accommodative monetary policy, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days, especially during a monetary easing cycle.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS decreases and S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of instances during an easing cycle, the hypothesis fails.
